content.snl: thm-hyp(list-partial(Type.judge(list-partial(@F, @G), Analysis.PFun), Type.judge(list-partial(@x, @L), Real), Analysis.funLim(F, @y, x, L), Logic.exists-typed(@delta, Real, Logic.and($#0 > 0$(delta), Logic.and(Set.subset(Analysis.nbhDel(x, delta), Analysis.domain(G)), Logic.forall-typed(@y, Real, Logic.implies(Set.mem(y, Analysis.nbhDel(x, delta)), Eq(Type.apply(Analysis.map(F), y), Type.apply(Analysis.map(G), y)))))))), Analysis.funLim(G, @y, x, L))
content.markdown:
If `F` tends to `L` at `x₀` and `G` agrees with `F` on some punctured neighbourhood of `x₀` (and that neighbourhood lies in `G`'s domain), then `G` tends to `L` at `x₀` as well. For sequences the corresponding statement is agreement beyond some index.

This is the precise sense in which a limit sees only germ-level data. It is also the workhorse lemma for rewriting under a limit, since it lets an algebraic simplification valid near `x₀` — but not at `x₀` — be applied.
